[element-institution-id]
=== `<institution-id>` Institution Identifier

A externally defined institutional identifier, whether organization-specific (for example, “IEEE”) or from an established identifying authority (for example, “Ringgold” or “ISNI”).

#### Usage/Remarks
##### Used with an Institutional Name

A wrapper element named <<element-institution-wrap,`<institution-wrap>`>> holds both the name of an institution (<<element-institution,`<institution>`>>) and any identifiers for that institution (<<element-institution-id,`<institution-id>`>>), for example, an INSI or Ringgold ID.
#### External Identifier

The <<element-institution-id,`<institution-id>`>> element holds an external identifier, assigned to an institution by a publisher, an archive or library, or an agency such as Ringgold or ISNI. The contents of this element should not be confused with the <<attribute-id,`@id`>> attribute, which holds an internal document identifier that can be used by software to construct a simple in-document link.
#### Multiple Identifiers

A single institution may have multiple identifiers, either because different assigning agencies have defined an identifier or because the entity belongs to more than one larger organizational unit, for example, a laboratory may be part of multiple institutions.
##### Common Practice

All levels of a multi-tier organization may be listed within a single <<element-institution,`<institution>`>> element and given a single institution identifier. For example, a program, a department, and a university may be part of the same <<element-institution,`<institution>`>>, inside a single <<element-institution-wrap,`<institution-wrap>`>> with a single `<institution-id>`. Similarly both a corporation and a division within the corporation might be inside one <<element-institution,`<institution>`>> element, inside a <<element-institution-wrap,`<institution-wrap>`>> with a single institution identifier (`<institution-id>`). Alternatively, a divisional distinction such as an “organization” element with a subordinate “dept” and an “office” inside a department could tagged using multiple <<element-institution,`<institution>`>> elements with the <<attribute-content-type,`@content-type`>> attribute differentiating institution, department, and office. Each of these divisions could be assigned an institutional identifier (`<institution-id>`), which would require the wrapper element <<element-institution-wrap,`<institution-wrap>`>>.
